newsitem.title: UK: City body examines potential for UK junk bonds.
newsitem.headline: City body examines potential for UK junk bonds.

text.p: City Promotion Panel, a London-based financial body, is looking at the prospects for a high-yielding bond, or 'junk bond' market in Britain, Economic Secretary to the Treasury, Angela Knight said on Monday.

The capital markets focus group of the City Promotion Panel is investigating the legal and regulatory framework needed for such a market, and industry attitudes which have so far inhibited the growth of a high-yielding debt market in the UK.
"The group is trying to identify why a high-yielding debt market works in other countries and examining the regulatory requirements," Knight said.
Speaking at the launch of a new leaflet publicising Britain's financial services industry, she noted: "There are some good opportunities there and we need to see if we can identify a need."
The capital market focus group was also considering holding an industry conference later this year to explore the results of its study on junk bonds, Knight said.
Investor demand for junk bonds is concentrated in the U.S. which possesses the only liquid market for such issues.

The City Promotion Panel was set up a year ago to co-ordinate the marketing of London's financial district. Among the official members are Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke and Governor of the Bank of England Eddie George.
